To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PRE applications of paraquat and residual (preplant incorporated) herbicides are required for effective Palmer amaranth control.

(1) PRE herbicides containing both paraquat and a residual herbicide(s), applied to winter wheat 2 WAP double crop soybean, provide excellent Palmer amaranth (A. palmeri) control 2 and 8 WAP soybean, and (2) 2,4-D and/or flumioxazil, applied preharvest to winter wheat, do not provide consistent Palmer amaranth control in soybean.

1) PRE treatments that include paraquat and residual (preemergence) herbicide(s) provide excellent early season Palmer amaranth control in double crop soybeans and 2) PRE herbicide programs that contain paraquat and residual provide excellent early season common waterhemp control in double crop beans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of herbicide programs for the control of glyphosate resistant Palmer amaranth (A. palmeri) in double crop soybeans after winter wheat in Kansas.
the development of a non glyphosate herbicid
the identification of effective herbicide programs for the management of glyphosate resistant Palmer amaranth in double crop soybeans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of sequential herbicide applications of glyphosate for control of glyphosate resistant Palmer amaranth (A. palmeri) in double crop soybeans after winter wheat has become economically and environmentally impractical.
the use of sequential glyphosate applications is no longer a viable option in glyphosate resistant double crop soybean due to the presence of glyphosate resistant Palmer amaranth.
the results indicate that Palmer amranth and waterhempt control was 85 or greater 8 weeks after planting for PRE treatments that contained a combination of paraquat and residual herbicides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are a variety of herbicide options available for the control of both Palmer amaranth or waterhemp in a double crop soybean system.
there is no single herbicide treatment or herbicide program that will consistently provide acceptable control of both Palmer amaranth (PA) and common waterhempt (CW).

we have found that PRE herbicide applications that contain both a residual herbicide and paraquat are the only treatments to consistently provide acceptable control of Palmer amranth and common waterhep in double crop soybeans after wheat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can control both Palmer amaranth (AMAPA) and common waterhempt (AMATA) if we use a residual herbicide (e.g., pyroxasulfon, pendimethalin) in combination with a non glyphosate herbicides.
we can still get good control with PRE applications, but we need to use multiple modes of action and multiple sites of action.
there is no one size fits all approach to managing Palmer amaranth.
